newsitem.title: CHINA: China may be forced to free oil, gas prices -paper.
newsitem.headline: China may be forced to free oil, gas prices -paper.

text.p: Pressure is mounting on China's government to ease decades of control over crude oil and natural gas prices, especially after the setting up of a third ministerial level oil firm, state media said on Sunday.

National Star Petroleum Corp, China's new state-owned oil company, is authorised to participate in onshore and offshore projects and to solicit foreign capital, breaking the monopoly of China National Petroleum Corp and China National Offshore Oil Corp.
However, it was not yet clear if National Star would be permitted to sell at international market prices, the China Daily Business Weekly said.
Industry insiders say they believe state price controls will be lifted soon.

In 1995, the government decided to free oil and gas prices within three years, but the latest information indicates price controls may not end so soon because of fears of inflation, the newspaper said.
The government must also decide who would allocate oil-bearing blocks to the three oil firms for exploration and development, the newspaper said.

The State Planning Commission currently receives such applications and issues licences, but this function is expected to be handed over to the Ministry of Geology and Mineral Resources, which is responsible for National Star, the newspaper said.
The addition of the third company was expected to boost competition and market forces in the industry, it said.
The three big oil firms might be forced to transform into enterprises independent of the government as competition grows, the newspaper said.
